messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Esperanto, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Esperanto line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (truth‑conditions) | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|------------------------------------------|----------------------|-----------------------|--------| | **ove** | locative subordinator “where” introducing a clause | **kie** | “where” | OK | | **udirai** | future action: the addressee will hear the shrieks | **aŭdos** | “will hear” | OK | | **le** | definite article, fem. pl., marks *strida* as specific | **la** | “the” | OK | | **disperate** | adjective qualifying *strida* as desperate | **malesperajn** | “despairing” | OK | | **strida** | plural noun, the shrieks that will be heard | **kriojn** | “shrieks” | OK | | **vedrai** | future action: the addressee will see the spirits | **vidos** | “will see” | OK | | **li** | definite article, masc. pl., marks *spiriti* as specific | **la** | “the” | OK | | **antichi** | adjective indicating great age (ancient) | **antikvajn** | “ancient” | OK | | **spiriti** | plural noun, the spirits that will be seen | **spiritojn** | “spirits” | OK | | **dolenti** | adjective describing the spirits as sorrowful | **dolorajn** | “woeful” | OK | | **ch’** (che) | relative pronoun introducing a clause about the spirits | **kiuj** | “who/which (plural)” | OK | | **a** | preposition “to, toward” introducing the object of the shout | **al** | “to/toward” | OK | | **la** | definite article, fem. sg., marks *morte* as specific | **la** | “the” | OK | | **seconda** | ordinal adjective “second” modifying *morte* | **dua** | “second” | OK | | **morte** | noun, the death that is the target of the shout | **morto** | “death” | OK | | **ciascun** | distributive quantifier “each” applying to the spirits | **ĉiu** | “each” | OK | | **grida** | present‑tense verb “shouts, cries out” performed by each spirit | **krias** | “shouts / cries out” | OK |
---
### Items to Review - **MISSING:** none - **WRONG:** none - **GRAMMAR:** none (agreement of adjectives and nouns is correct) - **UNNECESSARY:** none (all source words have a necessary counterpart in Esperanto)

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Esperanto script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Esperanto text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
